questions.q: Annotated diagram of spit formation, then: (a) Explain how a bar forms. (3) (b) Suggest why spits are important to people. (3)
questions.a: (a) spit grows across a bay, enclosing a lagoon (b) shelter harbours, habitats, tourism, protect land behind
questions.model: Teacher annotates the longshore drift arrows first.

questions.q: Use a satellite image of Spurn Head to describe its shape with a scale.
questions.a: Length about 5 km, curved tip, salt marsh behind

questions.q: Why might a spit be breached?
questions.a: Storm surges break through the narrow neck; reduced sediment supply

questions.q: Describe the features of a spit.
questions.a: Long, narrow ridge of sand or shingle (1) attached to land at one end (1), often with a curved (recurved) end and salt marsh behind (1)
questions.model: Shape: long, narrow. Attachment: one end on land. Tip: curved. Behind: salt marsh.
